source: GeoNames CC BY 4.0 modern P-class city coordinates and ID; Store norske leksikon, Larousse, Nizhny Novgorod Encyclopedia, Krasnodar municipality, Kemerovo Regional Scientific Library; separate preliminary sources are not approved.
selection: 25 distinct major Russian regional cities excluding Moscow, Saint Petersburg and Kaliningrad already staged; new records require independent historical evidence before release.
coordinateConvention: Current GeoNames WGS84 EPSG:4326 populated-place representative point, not historical city polygon.
countryCodeSemantics: RU is present-day GeoNames metadata only, never a historical sovereignty attribution.
historicNameScope: Only dated attested sustained official city names are published. Year-only histories stay year-granularity. 1801 baselines of A cities are provisional editorial projections.
reviewMethod: Compared all 264 previously staged GeoNames IDs in batches 01–22. Cross-checked source name eras and independent references for 10 approved B/C cities. Held modern-name-only cities and unresolved historical identity/orthography cases.
qualityNotes: All 25 IDs absent from earlier 264 staged IDs; none is a military base or individual facility.

10 B/C cases have independently cited naming change histories; 12 A cases are historical baselines from present-day GeoNames and not eligible for approval; 3 additional B/C investigations remain held.

Novosibirsk: 1903 city status; 1926-02-12 decree originally spelled Ново-Сибирск with hyphen. Current Новосибирск spelling's precise legal transition is unresolved; hold city until name-era fidelity checked.
Kyzyl: 1914 Belotsarsk, the unimplemented Uryankhaysk change proposal in 1918, and Khem-Beldyr naming chronology need archival reconciliation; do not promote.
Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk: historical Vladimirovka village and Toyohara city may not be identical urban entity, and 1905 Japanese annexation is not an exact city naming date; hold.
Kemerovo: Kemerovo Regional Scientific Library confirms Shcheglovsk city and decree on 1932-03-27; don't equate early Shcheglovo village with town.
Nizhny Novgorod: 1932-10-07 Gorky and 1990-10-22 Nizhny Novgorod from regional urban encyclopedia.
Krasnodar: city municipality records rename from Yekaterinodar effective 1920-12-07.
Murmansk: city founded 1916 Romanov-na-Murmane; 1917 name changed; year only.
1941–1945 or Russian Civil War occupations do not imply city name change; past governmental jurisdiction and urban tier must be separately sourced.
Approved source IDs are an explicit allowlist; no automatic expansion from provisional candidates.
No `main` merges, deployment, mobile app changes or candidate predicate changes.
